_comment: MOCK RUNTIME SCENARIO, not live output. Pins what each agent returns in scripts/workflow_dryrun.mjs so the mocked run follows the shape the synthetic fixture should produce (the answer key in expect.json). Used for mock-derived agent counts and the checker tests; it says nothing about how a live model behaves.

references.text: Roediger, H. L., III, & Karpicke, J. D. (2006). Test-enhanced learning: Taking memory tests improves long-term retention. Psychological Science, 17(3), 249-255.
Cohen, J. (1994). A power primer. Psychological Bulletin, 112(1), 155-159.

Marchetti-Oyelaran, T., & Lindqvist, H. (2021). Spaced retrieval lattices and examination performance in introductory courses: A fourteen-university replication. Journal of Applied Retrieval Science, 9(2), 113-131.

claims.claim: Roediger and Karpicke (2006) showed that retrieval practice doubled final-exam grades in university statistics courses [1].
Under conventional benchmarks, d = 0.2, 0.5 and 0.8 are small, medium and large effects [2].
A recent multi-site replication reported that spaced retrieval schedules raised introductory-course exam scores by 12 points across 14 universities [3].
The quiz section outperformed the re-read section by almost eight points, a medium effect by conventional benchmarks [2].
Retrieval practice works in the laboratory [1].
